Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
154 AM EST Tue Nov 24 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
High Wind Watch In Effect 10 am Thursday through 1 am Friday
Long Island and NYC metro. 

Storm Watch in Effect 6 am Thursday through 1 am Friday on
the coastal waters. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Cool and dry conditions expected through midweek.

2) A storm system impacts the area Thanksgiving into Friday 
with rain and strong to damaging winds.

3) Widespread coastal flooding along with beach flooding, erosion, 
and overwash possible Thursday into Friday. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Much cooler weather on tap for Tuesday and Wednesday as an 
anomalously strong 1040+ mb high builds from the Great Lakes
to New England. Temperatures will struggle to reach 50 degrees 
with highs topping out in the upper 40s. The coldest night of 
the season so far is expected tonight with temperatures 
bottoming out in the mid to upper 20s inland and upper 20s to 
low 30s most elsewhere. The NYC metro should remain just above 
freezing in the mid 30s. Similar conditions are expected on 
Wednesday, though cloud cover begins to increase late in the day
into the night ahead of approaching low pressure from the 
south. Lows Wednesday night will still be chilly, but not as low
as Tuesday due to the increasing E flow and mostly cloudy 
skies.


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
Strong to damaging winds along with steady moderate to locally
heavy rain are main concerns from an impactful storm
Thanksgiving into a portion of Friday. See Key Message 3
discussion for details on potential coastal flooding impacts

There are still some timing differences for when the strongest 
winds and widespread rain will arrive. Otherwise, the guidance 
is in good agreement with the low tracking north from the 
Carolina coast on Thursday. The low will likely stay just inland
from somewhere just west of the I-95 corridor to along the 
spine of the Appalachians. This potential difference does not 
change the potential wind and coastal impacts.

The main hazard will be from strong wind gusts with potential 
of damaging wind gusts, especially Long Island and NYC metro. 
The pressure gradient between departing high pressure and the 
approaching low will set up a corridor of potent low level winds
with progged 925 mb winds 60-70 kt. There is an inversion that 
will likely set up around 950 mb, but winds just beneath the 
inversion may range from 50-60 kt. BUFKIT soundings indicate 
mixing potential up to around 975 mb at times late morning 
through the Thanksgiving evening. Low level winds should start 
weakening sometime at night. The strongest winds in the mixed 
layer look to occur across Long Island into the NYC metro. SSTs 
in the mid to upper 50s may also allow the mixed layer to become
unstable enough for some of the higher winds to mix down. 
Thinking these ingredients support potential of E gusts up to 60
mph. For these reasons, have issued a High Wind Watch for Long 
Island, NYC metro, and E Essex, E Union, and Hudson County. Have
padded the timing for now given the uncertainty, so the watch 
is from 10 am Thursday through 1 am Friday. The period of 
highest winds may end up being in the afternoon and early 
evening. There is mot enough confidence to go with the watch 
further inland across CT, interior NE NJ, and Lower Hudson 
Valley. Will let the day shift reassess the need for an 
expansion if confidence/guidance continues to trend toward 
higher wind potential. Either way, additional zones may 
eventually need a wind advisory as the event draws near. 

Winds will weaken considerably late Thursday night into early
Friday as the low moves to the north. Gusts should increase 
again on Friday as the gradient increases behind the storm with 
potential of W gusts 25-35 mph.

A period of steady moderate, locally heavy, rainfall is expected 
with this event. The rain should start overspreading the area from 
the south in the morning, becoming steadier and heavier into the 
afternoon and evening. The slower guidance would have the rain 
starting in the afternoon. Rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches 
continue to be forecast. Locally higher amounts up to 3 inches 
cannot be ruled out, but this would be isolated. The fast movement 
of the system should preclude any significant flooding, but minor 
urban and poor drainage flooding is possible. The rain should taper 
off late Thursday night into early Friday. 

.KEY MESSAGE 3...
Coastal flooding is also growing more likely with a full moon on
the 24th and king tides this week. Given high astrotides, many 
locations need less than a foot to reach minor coastal flood 
benchmarks. Localized minor coastal flooding is possible with 
Wednesday morning's high tide. Then, the current forecast 
supports widespread minor to moderate flooding Thursday morning 
through Friday morning. Localized major is a possibility for the
most vulnerable locations of the south shore back bays and 
western Great South Bay. There are also a few spots in NE NJ 
such as Kearney Point and Hackensack River that are being 
watched for localized major coastal flooding. Some guidance, 
such as Stevens, has increased the potential for localized major
flooding. In the end, this will be determined by how fast the 
low tracks up the coast and how far inland of a track it takes. 
This will determine just how long we stay in E/NE flow before 
switching over to S/SW. In addition, beach flooding, erosion, 
and overwash would all be on the table. For now, the risk of 
overwash appears isolated, but this could change depending on 
how the system trends.

&&

.AVIATION /07Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
A cold front moves further offshore overnight with high pressure 
building through Tuesday night.

VFR throughout the TAF period.

Most city terminals and some coastal terminals should hold gusts in 
the 15 to 20 kt range much of the night. Winds increase towards the 
tail end of the Tue AM push with gusts in the 15-25kt range for the 
late morning and early afternoon. Gusts persist until around 20-21z.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Wind gusts may be more occasional at times overnight for KLGA, KJFK, 
and KEWR.

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z Wednesday through Saturday... 

Tuesday night: VFR. Light N winds.

Wednesday: VFR with winds NE. 

Thanksgiving: Rain developing with IFR. E winds 15-25kt G30-40kt. 
Peak gusts potentially higher. LLWS possible with 50+kt at 1000ft.

Friday: MVFR. W winds gusting to 25-35 kt. 

Saturday: MVFR possible with W winds gusting to 20-30 kt.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
SCA conditions will persist on the ocean through this evening
with lingering 5 ft seas and some wind gusts around 25 kt. 
Conditions should subside below Advisory levels this evening. 

A brief lull in SCA conditions is then expected into Wednesday 
before conditions start to ramp up Wednesday night ahead of an 
approaching low pressure from the south. Gusts quickly reach
gale and then potentially storm force on all waters Thursday 
into Thursday evening. The timing of the highest winds are still
a bit uncertain, and may occur in the afternoon and evening. 
Have issued a storm watch to cover this potential for Thursday 
into the first half of Thursday night. Gale gusts are then 
possible on Friday and Friday night, especially on the ocean., 
behind the departing storm. Winds should start subsiding on 
Saturday. 

Max significant wave heights could reach up to 15-20 ft on the
ocean and occasionally to 20-25 ft out east, 7-10 ft across LI 
Sound and around 10 ft on western Block Island Sound E of Orient
Point. Seas slowly subside Friday into the weekend, but may 
remain 5-8 ft on the ocean during the day Saturday.
